claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/ProductsController.cs lines 13-20: `[HttpGet] public async Task<ActionResult<List<ProductDto>>> List() { var products = await db.Products.Select(p => new ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.PriceVnd)).ToListAsync(); return Ok(products); }` - one return, no `if`, no Count/Any check. Live: `curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products` on the running stage-1 lab returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body a JSON array of 8 products.

Source lines 22-28: `[HttpGet("{id:int}")] ... var product = await db.Products.FindAsync(id); if (product is null) return NotFound(); return Ok(new ProductDto(product.Id, product.Name, product.PriceVnd));` - the NotFound() return precedes the only `new ProductDto(...)` on the success path. Live: /api/v1/products/1 -> 200 with one product object; /api/v1/products/999999 -> 404, so FindAsync returned null for the absent row.

The whole class body (lines 10-29) contains only `db.Products.Select(...).ToListAsync()` and `db.Products.FindAsync(id)`. No Add, Update, Remove, Attach, SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync, ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete appears anywhere in the file.

Ran the stage-1 lab (docker compose up -d --build --wait lab web db api) and curled through Caddy on 8080. /api/v1/products/1 -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, body one product object. /api/v1/products/999999 -> `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`, `Content-Type: application/problem+json; charset=utf-8`, body {"type":"https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9110#section-15.5.5","title":"Not Found","status":404,"traceId":"..."} - no product fields.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-1 lab, curl -i, 2026-09-24 (Caddyfile: handle /api/v1/* -> reverse_proxy api:8080)

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 9.2.1: "Request methods are considered 'safe' if their defined semantics are essentially read-only; i.e., the client does not request, and does not expect, any state change on the origin server as a result of applying a safe method to a target resource." and "the GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE methods are defined to be safe." 9.2.2: "Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent." Safe implies idempotent, so safe is the stronger promise.

No pinned document states a collection GET is "never a 404". It follows from RFC 9110 15.5.5 only while the collection resource itself exists: "The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists." An empty array is a current representation of an existing collection, so 404 would be wrong; but nothing in the spec ties 404 to item URLs. Live proof of the other case: GET /api/v1/products/abc (no matching route) answered 404 with no body.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: collection GET stays `200` - a collection URL names the whole set, and an empty set is still a representation of it, so the row count never turns the answer into a `404` (a URL that names no collection at all is a different case: there is nothing there to represent).

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 15.5.5: "The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists. A 404 status code does not indicate whether this lack of representation is temporary or permanent; the 410 (Gone) status code is preferred over 404 if the origin server knows ... that the condition is likely to be permanent." Both halves of the claim are literal in that paragraph.

Prepending is documented: "The route templates you define on the controller are prepended to route templates on the actions." (mvc/controllers/routing.md:414), so [Route("api/v1/products")] + [HttpGet] = GET /api/v1/products, + [HttpGet("{id:int}")] = /api/v1/products/{id}. But `int` is not "a whole number": the constraint table gives `{id:int}` example values "123456789, -123456789", "Matches any integer". Live: /api/v1/products/-1 reached Get (404 application/problem+json), while /api/v1/products/abc and /1.5 matched no route (404, no body).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]` above `Get(int id)` answers that same URL followed by an integer (a negative one matches too), which arrives as the `id` parameter; a segment that is not an integer, like `/api/v1/products/abc`, matches no route at all.

issues.text: "record, in the database, that a product was viewed" is the case RFC 9110 9.2.1 excludes from the safe-method rule: "most servers append request information to access log files at the completion of every response, regardless of the method, and that is considered safe". A view record in its own table is that bookkeeping, not a change to the product the client asked to read - so keyed answer (a) holds only if the view count sits on the product row - which the question never says. The lesson narrows its rule to "the resource the client asked to read", so a literal reader can defend (b).
issues.fix: Make the write land on the served resource: change the context to "also increment a `view_count` column on that product's own row - inside the same GET method, before returning the result", and option (a) to "...; incrementing `view_count` changes the very product row the client asked to read". Leave b/c/d unchanged.
issues.quote: A teammate wants `Get(int id)` to also record, in the database, that a product was viewed

issues.text: "never a `404`" (section 3, repeated in summary line 2) states a REST convention as an absolute rule. RFC 9110 15.5.5 ties 404 to "did not find a current representation for the target resource" and nowhere distinguishes collection URLs from item URLs; the lesson's own ledger admits this (claim 6: "This is a REST convention, not an HTTP-mandated rule") while the lesson text does not. A collection-shaped URL that names nothing at all does answer 404 - verified in the lab: GET /api/v1/products/abc returns 404.
issues.fix: Add the condition that carries the rule, in section 3 and summary line 2: the collection exists either way, so an empty array is still a representation of it and the row count never turns the answer into `404`. Claim 6's suggested_text can be used verbatim.
issues.quote: whatever the row count, an empty set is still a successful answer, never a `404`

issues.text: "`ToListAsync()` returns every product row" is not what that line does: the query is `db.Products.Select(p => new ProductDto(...)).ToListAsync()`, so what comes back is a `List<ProductDto>` - one DTO per product row, built from three columns - not the rows. The next sentence hangs the status code on that list, so the imprecision propagates.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "`ToListAsync()` runs the query and hands back one `ProductDto` per product row, and `FindAsync(id)` hands back the one row with that id, or `null` if there is none."

issues.text: "followed by a whole number" misstates the `{id:int}` constraint, documented as "Matches any integer" with example values `123456789, -123456789`. Confirmed in the lab: `/api/v1/products/-1` reaches `Get` (404 with a problem+json body, i.e. FindAsync ran), while `/api/v1/products/abc` matches no route (404 with no body) - two different 404s the lesson as written cannot tell apart.
issues.fix: Replace "a whole number" with "an integer (a negative one matches too)" and add that a segment which is not an integer, `/api/v1/products/abc`, matches no route rather than reaching `Get`.
issues.quote: answers that same URL followed by a whole number, which arrives as the `id` parameter
